Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.
At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company – we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.
As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.
Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.

The Role

As a University Recruiter at Veeva, you will be a critical growth driver for our Consultant Development Program (CDP) across the United Kingdom, Germany, and Spain.
In this role, you will lead top-of-funnel candidate attraction, source diverse early careeer talent, build relationships with leading European institutions, and deliver an exceptional candidate pre-boarding experience. You will operate with speed, focus, and a high level of individual accountability—embodying our core values of Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed.

What You'll Do

  • Proactive Sourcing & Outreach: Identify and engage top-tier early-career talent across Western Europe. Direct sourcing, referral channels, and targeted outreach in partnership with Talent Marketing
  • Assessment & Regional Alignment: Review and process candidate applications
  • Campus Partnerships & Events: Plan, attend, and execute university career events, technical fairs, and campus info sessions across target locations to position Veeva as an employer of choice
  • Community & Referral Pipeline: Build and nurture a dedicated, long-term referral pipeline across internal employee networks, university alumni groups, and student organizations
  • Pre-boarding & Candidate Engagement: Drive high-touch candidate engagement from offer acceptance to start date. Host monthly candidate touchpoints, facilitate cohort networking, and maximize early network visibility
  • Continuous Improvement: Embody our Care, Notice, Act philosophy by continuously evaluating sourcing channels, iterating digital campaigns, and optimizing hiring processes to keep things simple and highly effective

Requirements

  • Experience: 3+ years of talent acquisition experience with a strong focus on early-career or university recruiting across European markets
  • Location: Must be based and work-authorized in the United Kingdom
  • Execution Mindset: Relentless focus on execution, focus, and operational excellence. You take pride in moving fast with accuracy
  • Communication: Clear, concise, and humble communication style with strong stakeholder management abilities
  • Data & Process Focus: Comfortable using candidate assessment tools, tracking metrics, and driving structured weekly pipeline stand-ups

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience recruiting for software, cloud, or technical consulting services
  • Familiarity with regional university ecosystems across Western Europe
  • Experience partnering closely with Talent Marketing to build digital talent campaigns

Interviewing with Veeva

    We value your time and believe in a transparent hiring process. Here is the process you can expect.
  • Follow the application process and submit your resume.
  • Within 3 days, you will receive a link to a personality assessment administered by a third party.
  • Once you complete the assessment, our team will review your full application package and follow up via email with our decision.
  • If moving to the interview stage, the process is as follows:
    1. A conversation with the hiring manager
    2. A practical case exercise
    3. A final conversation with our group's Senior Leader.
  • Once all interviews are complete, the manager will be in touch with a final decision.
Veeva’s headquarters is located in the San Francisco Bay Area with offices in more than 15 countries around the world.
As an equal opportunity employer, Veeva is committed to fostering a culture of inclusion and growing a diverse workforce. Diversity makes us stronger. It comes in many forms. Gender, race, ethnicity, religion, politics, sexual orientation, age, disability and life experience shape us all into unique individuals. We value people for the individuals they are and the contributions they can bring to our teams.
If you need assistance or accommodation due to a disability or special need when applying for a role or in our recruitment process, please contact us at .

About Abridge

Abridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare. Our AI-powered platform was purpose-built for medical conversations, improving clinical documentation efficiencies while enabling clinicians to focus on what matters most—their patients.

Our enterprise-grade technology transforms patient-clinician conversations into structured clinical notes in real-time, with deep EMR integrations. Powered by Linked Evidence and our purpose-built, auditable AI, we are the only company that maps AI-generated summaries to ground truth, helping providers quickly trust and verify the output. As pioneers in generative AI for healthcare, we are setting the industry standards for the responsible deployment of AI across health systems.

We are a growing team of practicing MDs, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to empower people and make care make more sense. We have offices located in the Mission District in San Francisco, the SoHo neighborhood of New York, and East Liberty in Pittsburgh.

The Role

Early talent is one of the highest-leverage investments we can make in Abridge's future. We are looking for a University Recruiter to help us identify and hire exceptional emerging talent with the ability, drive, and mission alignment to build meaningful careers here.

We want to create an early talent program that reaches broadly and assesses people for their potential, not only their pedigree. That includes exceptional candidates from leading universities as well as community colleges, bootcamps, apprenticeships, career transitions, and other paths.

You will partner closely with our Early Talent Program Manager and engineering leaders to build this capability from the ground up. You will own recruiting for interns and early career talent, primarily across software engineering, while helping us expand into other functions over time.

This is an opportunity for someone who loves recruiting, exercises strong judgment, and is energized by building a program—not simply inheriting one.

This role is based in our San Francisco office and requires being in the office three days per week.

What You’ll Do

  • Own end-to-end intern and early career recruiting, initially focused on software engineering

  • Partner with our Early Talent Program Manager to build and execute a differentiated hiring strategy

  • Find exceptional candidates across universities, technical communities, bootcamps, apprenticeships, and other talent channels including event strategies

  • Work with engineering leaders to define exceptional potential and build a rigorous, consistent evaluation process

  • Deliver a candidate experience that reflects how we operate at Abridge: demanding, caring, and mission-driven

  • Use pipeline data and hiring outcomes to continually improve our approach

  • Build the systems and partnerships needed to scale the program

  • Support other critical technical roles outside peak early talent cycles

What You’ll Bring

  • Experience recruiting software engineers, ideally including interns or early career talent

  • A track record of finding strong candidates through a range of sourcing channels

  • Enough technical fluency to evaluate engineering profiles and partner credibly with hiring managers

  • Strong judgment for recognizing potential, learning velocity, and motivation beyond traditional credentials

  • A builder's mindset and comfort creating structure in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment

  • High ownership, urgency, and care for the candidate experience

  • Genuine connection to Abridge's mission and excitement about helping emerging talent begin their careers here

Bonus Points If…

  • You have built or scaled an early talent program

  • You have recruited across both technical and non-technical early career roles

  • You have developed partnerships with bootcamps, apprenticeships, community colleges, or other alternative talent communities

This is a hybrid role requiring a minimum of 3 days per week in our San Francisco office, with flexibility for remote work on other days.

Why Work at Abridge?

At Abridge, we’re transforming healthcare delivery experiences with generative AI, enabling clinicians and patients to connect in deeper, more meaningful ways. Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month.

Joining Abridge means stepping into a fast-paced, high-growth startup where your contributions truly make a difference. Our culture requires extreme ownership—every employee has the ability to (and is expected to) make an impact on our customers and our business.

Beyond individual impact, you will have the opportunity to work alongside a team of curious, high-achieving people in a supportive environment where success is shared, growth is constant, and feedback fuels progress. At Abridge, it’s not just what we do—it’s how we do it. Every decision is rooted in empathy, always prioritizing the needs of clinicians and patients.

We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. Whether it's flexible work hours, an inclusive culture, or ongoing learning opportunities, we are here to help you thrive and do the best work of your life.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact alongside passionate people who care deeply about what they do, Abridge is the place for you.

How we take care of Abridgers:

  • Generous Time Off: 14 paid holidays, flexible PTO for salaried employees, and accrued time off for hourly employees

  • Comprehensive Health Plans: Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage for all full-time employees and their families.

  • Generous HSA Contribution: If you choose a High Deductible Health Plan, Abridge makes monthly contributions to your HSA.

  • Paid Parental Leave: Generous paid parental leave for all full-time employees.

  • Family Forming Benefits: Resources and financial support to help you build your family.

  • 401(k) Matching: Contribution matching to help invest in your future.

  • Personal Device Allowance: Tax free funds for personal device usage.

  • Pre-tax Benefits: Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Commuter Benefits.

  • Lifestyle Wallet: Monthly contributions for fitness, professional development, coworking, and more.

  • Mental Health Support: Dedicated access to therapy and coaching to help you reach your goals.

  • Sabbatical Leave: Paid Sabbatical Leave after 5 years of employment.

  • Compensation and Equity: Competitive compensation and equity grants for full time employees.

  • ... and much more!

Equal Opportunity Employer

Abridge is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants equally without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability.

We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the interview process. Once you submit your application, we'll follow up with details on how to request an accommodation for interviewing, completing any assessments, or otherwise participating in the selection process.

Staying safe - Protect yourself from recruitment fraud

We are aware of individuals and entities fraudulently representing themselves as Abridge recruiters and/or hiring managers. Abridge will never ask for financial information or payment, or for personal information such as bank account number or social security number during the job application or interview process. Any emails from the Abridge recruiting team will come from an @abridge.com email address. You can learn more about how to protect yourself from these types of fraud by referring to this article. Please exercise caution and cease communications if something feels suspicious about your interactions.

At The Intern Group, we believe in the power of potential. Our purpose is to inspire and encourage individuals to believe in and challenge themselves, discover their passions, and realize their true potential. Our vision is bold: a world where all 8 billion people can achieve their dreams. We are on a mission to make this vision a reality, aiming to welcome over 10,000 participants to our programs annually by 2030.

We aim to cultivate a future where international internships are a key component of academic journeys, with many participants supported by our scholarship program. This future will empower a new generation—skilled, globally-minded, and ready to lead with understanding and cooperation.

Guided by our core values—people focus, teamwork, continuous learning, and global leadership—The Intern Group has grown from a serendipitous meeting of our Co-Founders in a London pub to becoming the leading provider of international internships, receiving 40,000 applications annually. Join us in shaping the next generation of global leaders.

Does this sound like a place where you can grow? Want to be a part of our journey? Come join our team as:

YOUR IMPACT

Join us in our purpose to inspire the leaders of tomorrow!

We’re looking for a highly organized, proactive, and enthusiastic University Partnerships Intern to join our University Partnerships Team (UPT). You’ll work closely with a global team that manages relationships with 150+ universities and helps students access transformative international experiences.

This is a hands-on role where you’ll support the team across university engagement, alumni ambassador coordination, events, site visits, presentations, and marketing projects. You’ll have the opportunity to work with colleagues and partners around the world while developing practical experience in partnerships, international education, marketing, and project coordination.

The ideal person is someone who enjoys making things happen—someone who is organized, pays attention to detail, follows through on tasks, and can confidently manage multiple projects and deadlines.

YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support the UPT team with day-to-day coordination, projects, research, and administrative tasks that help the team achieve its partnership and enrollment goals.
  • Coordinate Alumni Ambassadors, supporting communication, engagement, scheduling, content collection, and ongoing program activities.
  • Support career fair and conference participation, including logistics, registrations, materials, presentations, meeting schedules, and follow-up.
  • Prepare university presentations and materials, helping the team deliver engaging and professional presentations to university partners and students.
  • Coordinate the logistics of university site visits, including scheduling, itineraries, materials, communication, and follow-up.
  • Support the marketing and distribution of UPT impact reports and other partner-facing materials, working with the marketing team where appropriate.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date information, including data clean-up and regular follow-ups, across the CRM, spreadsheets, and other team systems.
  • Support other UPT initiatives and projects as they arise, taking ownership of assigned tasks and ensuring they are completed on time.

YOUR SKILLS & REQUIREMENTS

  • A strong interest in international education, university partnerships, marketing, or global business.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
  • Strong organization and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines.
  • A proactive, positive, and can-do attitude.
  • Strong follow-through—you take ownership and make sure things get done.
  • Comfortable working independently in a remote environment while collaborating with a global team.
  • Confident using digital tools such as Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, Canva, or similar platforms.
  • Creative and resourceful, with an interest in creating engaging presentations and partner-facing materials.
  • Comfortable working with spreadsheets, databases, and CRM systems.
  • Previous experience in university, marketing, events, administration, student organizations, or customer-facing roles is a plus.
  • Experience studying, working, or living abroad is a plus.

YOU’LL LOVE WORKING AT TIG BECAUSE

At The Intern Group, we’re passionate about people, their growth, and making an impact. You’ll work alongside a diverse, global team and gain hands-on experience in international education and university partnerships.

You’ll have the opportunity to:

  • Work with a global team and international university partners.
  • Take ownership of meaningful projects from day one.
  • Develop skills across partnerships, events, marketing, project management, and communications.
  • Build an international professional network.
  • Learn from experienced colleagues across different areas of the business.
  • Contribute directly to our mission of inspiring the leaders of tomorrow.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive internship stipend
  • Generous global PTO policy
  • Continuous learning opportunities
  • Access to the Career Advancement Training course and the Keynote Speaker Series
  • The incredible opportunity to meet new people and network with people from all around the world across a wide range of industries.

Sound like a good fit?

Please select the “Apply for this Job” button and submit a brief cover letter (addressed to Johanna Molina) telling us a bit about yourself along with your resume/CV in English.

The Intern Group is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply. We know that statistically women and people of color are less likely to apply to a position where they do not meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to apply even if this is the case for you.

Are you curious about our history?

Listen to our co-founders, Johanna Molina, David Lloyd, and Lee Carlin, as they share insights into our journey and aspirations.

University Admissions Tutor & Advisor

Location: Remote
Employment type: Part-time, flexible and assignment-based
Compensation: $25 per hour.

About Brainlyne

Brainlyne supports students and families with international university applications and educational opportunities.

We are building a team of tutors and advisors to support students through online group classes and individual guidance. Our work covers university orientation, admissions preparation, and application support across different tracks, including the US, UK, Europe, and other destinations.

Areas we are hiring for

Depending on your background and preferences, you may support one or more of the following:

  • SAT and test preparation

  • English and academic writing

  • Essay brainstorming and feedback

  • University orientation and admissions systems

  • US, UK, and European application guidance

  • University research and school-list building

  • Activities, CVs, and personal profile development

  • Interview and financial-aid preparation

You do not need to cover every area. Assignments will be matched to your academic background, experience, strengths, and preferred areas of support.

Responsibilities

Online group classes

  • Lead engaging online sessions for groups of students

  • Teach topics such as SAT preparation, English, writing, and general university preparation

  • Explain university admissions systems, timelines, and requirements

  • Support students with practical exercises and clear next steps

Individual student support

  • Review each student’s personal Brainlyne folder and current progress

  • Follow an individual plan based on the student’s goals, destination, and stage of preparation

  • Support university lists, applications, essays, activities, CVs, interviews, and deadlines

  • Give constructive written and verbal feedback

  • Help students complete their own work without writing applications or essays for them

  • Track progress, update notes, and communicate important concerns to the Brainlyne team

Requirements

  • Currently enrolled as a junior or senior, or an alumnus or recent graduate of a leading university

  • Demonstrated experience in tutoring, teaching, mentoring, admissions advising, essay editing, writing support, or a related area

  • Strong knowledge of at least one relevant subject or admissions track

  • Strong written and spoken English

  • Excellent communication, organization, and follow-up skills

  • Comfortable teaching online and working with students independently

  • Reliable, patient, and able to provide thoughtful feedback

Candidates may come from universities such as Princeton, Harvard, Oxford, NYU, or other comparable institutions. However, university background alone is not enough. We are especially interested in candidates with practical experience supporting students.

Important expectations

Tutors and advisors must maintain professional boundaries. They should not write applications or essays on behalf of students, or guarantee admission, scholarships, visas, or test scores.

This is a flexible, assignment-based role. Compensation is based on approved hours completed and documented, including group classes, individual sessions, preparation, and feedback.

National University – San Diego, California

Part-time Faculty:University Support Provider - Bilingual Authorization

Location: Remote, USA

National University is a veteran-founded, San Diego-based nonprofit. Since 1971, our mission has been to provide accessible higher education to adult learners. Today, we educate a diverse student body from across the U.S. and around the globe, with more than 230,000 alumni worldwide. Our eight schools and two colleges offer more than 200 accredited and licensed graduate and undergraduate programs. National University holds accreditation through the Western Senior College and Universities Commission (WSCUC).

Position Summary

The Department of Teacher Education in the Sanford College of Education at the National University invites applications for part-time faculty in University Support Provider - Bilingual Authorization. The successful candidate will have a demonstrated record of or potential for excellence in teaching in their field and a commitment to serving the university’s diverse adult student body. The successful candidate will have the potential for a commitment to serving the university’s diverse adult student body. This position primarily works closely with the Academic Program Director and other faculty within the program and contributes to ensuring program quality, student engagement, and success.

Essential Job Duties:

  • Provide substantive, timely feedback to students on various assessment activities.
  • Maintain a positive, safe, inclusive student-centric learning environment.
  • Complete required tasks on deadlines (e.g., final grades, assessment, grading rubrics, input for grade appeals, etc.)
  • Maintain appropriate professional training and/or scholarly activities, when applicable.
  • Provide feedback to the course lead regarding the course content.
  • Identify at-risk students and collaborate with student services.

Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in the field of Education, with active California credential required.
  • 3 years of higher education teaching experience preferred.
  • Must hold either a multiple subject or single subject in California AND a Bilingual Authorization to be considered.

For full consideration, interested candidates should provide the following:

  • A cover letter.
  • A curriculum vita.
  • Statement of teaching experience online and/or onsite for a diverse student body.

Candidate receiving offers will be offered a salary/pay rate commensurate with experience that vary based on a candidate’s qualifications, skills, and competencies. Absent exceptional circumstances, candidates will be offered a salary within this range for this position. Regional Director, University Relations (14 openings)

About Juno

Juno organizes the buying power of admitted and current students to negotiate lower cost private loan options, at no cost to schools or students. Students simply join a waitlist, Juno secures discounts that are better than going directly to lenders, and students can check rates with no impact to their credit. We also provide 1:1 advising to thousands of students each year, helping them compare options with confidence.

  • Since 2018, Juno has helped 290k+ students and families access over $2B in funding at the lowest rates available.
  • In 2025, we estimate 14–15% of all private in‑school graduate lending flowed through Juno and are growing rapidly;

We are the most popular way to find a private student loan for the world's top graduate programs, and we're looking for a team to help the financial aid offices understand the value we bring to students and families.

The Problem

Federal lending reforms have created a significant market shift. In July 2026, new caps on federal graduate loans, including the elimination of Grad PLUS for new students, came into effect, leaving millions of students with significant funding gaps. Students need transparent, competitive private options — exactly what Juno provides.

When a student hits that gap, they may ask a financial aid administrator. If that administrator has never heard of Juno, the student may never hear about us either.

Your mission

We're seeking up to fourteen Regional Directors, each owning one territory. Your job is to (i) ensure the administrators are aware about Juno, (ii) trust Juno enough that their students are also made aware about Juno (through numerous means such as direct mention by an administrator, getting Juno listed as a resource on a school's website, into a school's webinar calendar, and/or admitted student and current student communications). We expect you to thoroughly evaluate Juno to ensure you understand us deeply, so you can answer any questions about Juno, how we operate and the outcomes our members have.

What you'll do

  • Own a territory: Every financial aid office in it, and every relationship inside those offices. You build the plan, set the calendar, manage your budget and deliver results.
  • Build Relationships: Juno has tremendous value to add in the form of financial education and better loan products. Our model is different and we are not a lender. It can take time to gain full understanding and buy-in from the financial aid community. Keep showing up as a trustworthy voice.
  • Live in your associations: Membership, exhibiting, sessions, listservs, volunteer roles. This profession decides who's credible in person.
  • Get on campus: Conferences introduce; visits close. Six to eight campus swings a year.
  • Deliver webinars: Deliver institutional sessions from the standard deck. You don't have to write it, but you do have to practice it and run it like you did.
  • Keep your CRM true: Named contact, last touch, next step, on every active account. If it isn't in the CRM, it didn't happen.
  • Feed intel back: What competitors are offering, what's changing on campus, what students are actually asking. Product and marketing need it to help you succeed

Support our members: During peak borrowing season it’s all-hands-on-deck to ensure Juno members receive timely answers, 1:1 support, and the best customer service in the sector! You’ll likely be tapped to support member communications during peak.

  • Use AI as a multiplier: Institution research, RFI drafts, call prep, follow-up. Faster work, and you catch it when it's wrong.

What We Offer

Compensation: $115,000 plus $50k on-target bonus based on measurable, achievable outcomes.

Benefits: Comprehensive health, dental, vision, and 401(k) matching.

What We're Looking For

  • Background: 3+ years in financial aid administration, student lending sales, higher education partnerships, or a closely related role serving students. Having strong relationships within the financial aid/higher education sector is a must. Time in a financial aid office is valuable.

Ability to Prioritize: Understand where to focus your time and energy.

  • Consultative patience: A listing / webinar etc. can take several touches and time to establish trust.
  • You can present: To a room of aid administrators and to a room of students, on the same trip.
  • You can write: RFI and RFP responses are how schools judge whether we're serious.
  • Regulatory literacy: You can answer compliance and regulation questions accurately in the room without overpromising, and you escalate rather than improvise. We'll train you; you have to want to know.
  • Self-management: You build your own plan across dozens of institutions with no daily supervision, and you're honest in your own pipeline.
  • Curiosity about the product: You want to understand how student lending actually works — federal versus private, what drives a rate, cosigners, deferral, refinancing — because you can't advise an aid officer on a product you don't understand.
  • Comfort with seasonality: Fall and spring decide the year. You plan for them months ahead and go all-in when they land.
  • Location and travel: You live in your territory. Roughly 30% travel estimated (more or less depends on your execution), concentrated in those two seasons.

The X-Factor

  • You're the person they call: Aid officers ask your opinion on things you're not selling.
  • You're curious about the data: When a school says yes, your first instinct is to ask why — and whether the next school looks like it.
  • You close the loop: A campus visit isn't done until the notes are in the CRM and the next step has a date.
  • You're comfortable alone: You're the only Juno person in the building, and that's the part you like.

Why Join Juno?

The Opportunity

  • Real Impact: Help hundreds of thousands of students get access to the lowest rates on the market.
  • Market Timing: Federal aid changes create massive tailwind for growth.
  • Proven Model: $2B+ negotiated, 290K+ members.
  • Ground Floor: All new initiative. In most cases, you'll be the first Juno person your schools ever meet.
